findings.text: The delivered title's fourth line reads '... split 844.49 A in the 16 fitted-cut cells + 228.22 A in the 15 fully open cells', while the citing paragraph in docs/plans/forward-solve-api.html states 844.30 A in the sixteen fitted-cut cells and the pre-delivery receipt held 844.2978 A. Regenerating the census moved the fitted-cut split to 844.4895 A on unchanged nova code, so the committed panel no longer re-derives against the paragraph that cites it - the defect the driving followup f-fsa-repair-sol-ledger-panel was written to repair. The drift is disclosed in the evidence anchor and parked landing fragment but the paragraph was not reconciled, leaving two conflicting values for the same split in the record.

The gate reads its expected ampere split from the receipt it renders (counts = json.loads((RECEIPT / 'sol-ledger-census.json').read_text())['common_sol_split']), so it asserts only that the title agrees with the receipt the title was generated from. The SPEC's named check - the title contains the 1072.71 A and 844.30 A split - is unenforced: the gate stays green for any receipt content, including the 844.49 A that has drifted from the citing paragraph.

The plan landing record was not written (edit_plan refused a text edit inside a section[data-reckon] structured-state region) and is reported under a non-standard note: key while blockers: none is set. The recognised status vocabulary is complete / blocked / failed; a blocker stated only in a key the classifier does not read leaves the run looking clean, and the landing fragment sits at plan-landing-comment.html in the run directory, outside the repository, so plan state and code disagree.

justifications.durability: The evidence anchor (docs/evidence/archive/forward-solve-api-landed.html#sol-ledger-panel, 49 added lines) records the defect, the render-from-receipt path with its measured cost, the LIMITED-state reason for no saddle, the gate and the negative control, and the census drift paragraph in full - so a later reader can reconstruct what was delivered and why. The receipt carries the render payload and render_from_receipt makes the panel checkable without a solve, and the one-job rather than array discipline is stated. Two deductions. First, the plan landing record is not landed: the worker reports that edit_plan refused the text edit inside a section[data-reckon] structured-state region and parks the fragment at plan-landing-comment.html in the run directory rather than in-tree, so the plan state and the code do not yet agree and the reconciliation depends on a coordinator reading an out-of-tree file. Second, that unmet landing is reported under the non-standard note: key while blockers: none - a blocker in a key the manifest vocabulary does not recognise reads as no blocker to the classifier that gates promotion - and the panel now disagrees with the paragraph that cites it, left unreconciled in the delivered record. The plan value it should be reconciled against is 844.30 A in the sixteen fitted-cut cells (docs/plans/forward-solve-api.html, section 3 census comment), which the paragraph still states.
justifications.evidence: The gate log's first line names the revision (99bdb1a9a), the tree and the command, and its body reads 2 passed in 11.75s. The negative control is the declared mutation 'remove the draw_wall call' reproduced verbatim on its first line, and its body is genuinely red: the wall assertion drives wall_node_count to 0 exactly as the mutation promises. The render metrics are committed beside the figure (sol-ledger-render.json: wall 61 nodes / 1 unit, axis_drawn true, admitted_null_class wall_contact, strike_points_drawn 1, title widths against a 1728 px canvas), the PNG and SVG are committed under git add -f, and the receipt now carries a render payload with render_from_receipt plus --render-only so a reader can redraw the panel with no solve. One deduction, and it is structural: the title assertion in tests/test_sol_ledger_render.py derives the ampere split from the very receipt it renders (counts = json.loads((RECEIPT / 'sol-ledger-census.json').read_text())), so it asserts only that the title agrees with the receipt - it was regenerated from that receipt - and cannot detect drift away from the 1072.71 A / 844.30 A split the SPEC and the citing paragraph name. A gate that reads its expected value from the artifact under test is green by construction for this question.
justifications.fit: The delivered panel obeys the binding plotting rules and the compute hierarchy. 2D panel drawn with the axis off through the nova.media painters; the solved field is unfilled line contours (tricontour with colors='#999999', linewidths=0.35), never a filled map; draw_wall is called over the unit collection (units=(wall,)); draw_nulls marks the axis (solid triangle via variant(axis_marker='^')) and the admitted boundary nulls, and the receipt records the null class it admitted; the title is wrapped and measured line by line against the canvas before drawing, which is the specific repair the followup asked for on that clause. The census regeneration is one all_debug job with TMPDIR set in submit and payload, the shared interpreter called directly without uv on the compute node, and the render run on the login node from the receipt - the lane shape the brief and the repo AGENTS.md require (no array, no per-row job). Disclosed here rather than scored down: the driver's strike fallback (if not strike: strike = _finite_points(topology.wall_point)) is a rendering-input fallback justified by the node's first capture exporting an empty boundary-null set, which the gate then caught - the gate doing its job, correctly.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The followup f-fsa-repair-sol-ledger-panel asks for one repair: the committed panel must draw the wall over the unit collection, the axis and the admitted nulls, with a wrapped title whose lines do not cut off the 1072.71 A / 844.30 A split that 'does otherwise re-derive against the citing paragraph'. Three of four are delivered and checked: wall drawn via units=(wall,) (wall_node_count 61, wall_unit_count 1, closed), axis triangle drawn, admitted boundary nulls drawn through the draw_nulls strike slot with admitted_null_class wall_contact, and the four title lines measured against the canvas (widest 1488 px of 1728 px) so nothing is clipped. The node's reading of 'the admitted saddle' as the admitted boundary nulls for a LIMITED terminal state (topology_branch.x_point is NaN, so no saddle is admitted) is the reading the run's own resume advice ruled correct, not a deviation. But the fourth clause is not met in the delivered artifact: the citing paragraph at docs/plans/forward-solve-api.html still states 844.30 A in the sixteen fitted-cut cells, and the committed panel and receipt now carry 844.49 A, so the panel no longer re-derives against the paragraph it is cited against - which is precisely the defect the followup was written to remove. The node regenerated the census during delivery: the base receipt held 844.2978 A / 228.4138 A, the delivered receipt holds 844.4895 A / 228.2162 A, and the drift is disclosed in the evidence anchor and the parked landing fragment. Disclosure is not reconciliation, and the visible consequence is a delivered figure that disagrees with its own citing text.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat e1f123955 66bcde45c names only the seven declared paths: benchmarks/sol_ledger_current_census.py, tests/test_sol_ledger_render.py, docs/figures/forward-solve-api/sol-ledger-census/{sol-ledger-census.json, sol-ledger-current.png, sol-ledger-current.svg, sol-ledger-render.json} and docs/evidence/archive/forward-solve-api-landed.html. Nothing outside the declared write paths was written, no shared file was touched, and the working tree at the tip is clean. The one declared path the node did NOT write is docs/plans/forward-solve-api.html: the plan landing record is absent because edit_plan refused the insertion. That absence is honest scope behaviour under a tool refusal rather than an overreach, so the deduction is small, but the record it leaves behind (no in-tree landing; fragment parked outside the repo) is counted where it belongs, under durability.
